newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares higher in post-bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares higher in post-bourse trade.

text.p: German shares continued to move higher in afternoon post-bourse trade on Thursday, after chalking up solid gains on data which indicated slower than expected economic growth in the first quarter of the year.
At 1429 GMT the IBIS DAX index was up 24.80 points at 3,372.34 points, while June DAX DTB futures were up 23 points at 3,380 points.

Shares were also buoyed by advances in the German bond market, which remained firm after the Bundesbank decided to leave its key interest rates unchanged and statements at the Bundesbank's press conference were positively received.
Earlier the DAX index ended up 29.80 points at 3,383.25 points, building on a stable start in pre-bourse trade despite sharp declines on car giant Daimler-Benz.
Daimler was down 1.85 percent, or 2.50 marks, at 132.50 marks in late IBIS. It released 1996 earnings on Wednesday.
Dealers said some of Daimler's news, including plans for a convertible note issue, had proved disappointing, especially in the light of the recent rally among German car shares.
The overall market got a boost from a report showing the Ifo institute's business climate index fell to 92.4 in March from 93.6, far below expectations for a figure of around 94.0.
Shares in BMW, which has had a good run of late in common with other car stocks, were down 17 marks at 1,408 marks.
BMW chief Bernd Pischetsrieder said on Wedesday that BMW was expecting "slight" earnings growth in 1997, a comment he clarified as meaning single digit percent growth.
Airline Deutsche Lufthansa issued a statement from the company saying its 1997 results would be above those in 1996. Its shares fell 19 pfennigs to 22.40 marks.
